comparison: Perfect agreement on tumor suppressor findings (C2, C4, C24-C29, C61, C69). Both evaluations find the claims SUPPORTED with high confidence. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and sample sizes, while peer reviewers describe data as 'excellent quality' and 'convincing and justified.'

Disagreement on methylation assay findings (C31-C41, C63). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by multiple complementary assays, while peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 3's specific concerns about Figure 2F product distribution (C36, C39) and reproducibility questions about Figure 2B matching.

Agreement on polyacetylation effects (C3, C5, C44-C47). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate replication and statistical analysis, while peer reviewers describe the work as 'well-designed' with 'excellent quality data.' Both acknowledge the mechanistic interpretation (C47) as inferential.

Disagreement on position-specific acetylation and binding effects (C6, C48-C52, C66). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED and appropriately qualified as 'subtle,' while peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 3's challenge that binding differences in Figure 4E are 'minimal' and require quantification across multiple repeats.

Agreement on ubiquitination findings (C7, C56-C58, C67). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the use of three independent assays and appropriate controls, while peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'ubiquitination of H2A and H2B has no effect' and describe overall data quality as excellent.

OpenEval evaluates background/established knowledge claims (C1, C8-C23, C59-C60) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent contextual rather than novel experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluates prior work citations (C30, C42-C43, C53-C55, C62, C68) as SUPPORTED and appropriately contextualized. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these claims reference external studies rather than novel findings.

OpenEval rates speculative mechanistic hypotheses (C64-C65) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are appropriately presented as speculation without direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific speculative claims.
